set.body:
Raised by independent review while Epic 4 is in flight. This is the same criterion Epic 4 already accepted, applied to the kernel Epic 4 does not reserve.

Epic 4 delivered its criterion for the effect-form kernel

"Hot-loop object-size counters are replaced by static owned-buffer planning plus coarse execution observations."

Verified: R/kernel.R and R/task.R now contain ZERO object.size / .measured_object_bytes calls (they previously sat in the innermost loop body), and max_*_bytes fields in task.R are down from 17 to 2. Good.

The measurement-form kernel was not in the reservation and still has the pattern

1. HOT LOOP - measurement-kernel.R:332-339. Two utils::object.size() calls inside the per-feature-block loop opened at :327, itself inside the per-partition loop at :325:

     for (partition in relation$partitions)
       for (start in seq.int(1L, relation$n_features, by = feature_block))
         ...
         diagnostics$max_relation_block_bytes <- max(..., as.double(utils::object.size(relation_block)))
         diagnostics$max_factor_slice_bytes   <- max(..., as.double(utils::object.size(factor_slice)))

   Both quantities are known statically from the plan: relation_block is q x length(features) doubles and factor_slice is nrow(operator) x length(features) doubles. Nothing is being discovered by measuring.

2. PREFLIGHT ALLOCATES WHAT IT MEASURES - measurement-kernel.R:236-238:

     matrix_bytes <- function(rows, columns) as.double(utils::object.size(matrix(0, rows, columns)))

   This allocates a full zero matrix purely to ask how large it would be, and is called four times at :242-245 to size the relation buffer and factor slices. A memory preflight that allocates the buffers it is deciding whether it can afford is self-defeating: at q = 200 and feature_block = 20000 it allocates 32 MB per call, roughly 128 MB across the four, before reporting whether the plan fits.

   The arithmetic is exact and needs no allocation. Verified across shapes:

     matrix(0, 12, 50000)  object.size = 4800216   8*r*c + 216 = 4800216   identical
     matrix(0, 200, 20000) object.size = 32000216  8*r*c + 216 = 32000216  identical
     matrix(0, 3, 10)      object.size = 456       8*r*c + 216 = 456       identical

3. measurement-kernel.R:239-241 walks object.size over every measurement leg operator. Those are the dense p-wide leg operators, so this is a deep walk over the largest objects in the subsystem, purely for a diagnostic.

Line 634 is inside the benchmark harness and is fine where it is.

Suggested fix

Replace matrix_bytes with 8 * rows * columns + 216, derive the loop diagnostics from the plan rather than measuring per block, and keep coarse observed totals if they are wanted. This is the same change Epic 4 already made in kernel.R and task.R, so the two kernels end up consistent.

Not urgent and not a correctness defect. Filing so the measurement kernel does not silently keep the pattern the effect-form kernel just shed - it matters more here, because this is the subsystem that must eventually run at brain scale.
set.title: measurement-kernel retains hot-loop object.size instrumentation; its memory preflight allocates the buffers it is sizing
